results.summary: This design converts I2S audio input to PDM output using an inverted CIC filter and modulator. It also supports up to eight PDM microphones, producing per-microphone PCM outputs and a beamformed PCM output, with delay selection controlled by five pins. The design is intended for use with an I2S output device and PDM input devices, such as microphones and a clock generator. The documentation is minimal beyond the pin descriptions and a brief explanation of the core conversion method.

DemoSiine is a demoscene-style audio-visual project that generates a 640x480 VGA video signal and a looping ~28 second audio track. The video output includes dynamic wavy sine layers and a rainbowy overlay, with user controls to enable/disable layers, pause the animation, and toggle styles. The audio engine drives a frequency synthesizer to produce the soundtrack. It requires external hardware: a TinyVGA PMOD for video output, a TT Audio PMOD for audio output, and switches for input control.

The donut project displays a rendered donut on a VGA screen. It uses hand-crafted ellipses to create the donut shape and outputs a standard VGA signal with 2-bit RGB color, horizontal sync, and vertical sync. The design operates with a 50.35 MHz clock and requires a TinyVGA PMOD connected to the output pins for display. The documentation is sparse, providing only a brief description and testing instructions.

This analog project provides three building blocks: a low-dropout regulator (LDO), a bandgap current reference, and an oscillator. The LDO output and oscillator output are accessible on pins, and the oscillator can be enabled and reset via digital inputs. Silicon test reports indicate the LDO outputs around 1.8V and the oscillator runs at approximately 5.2-5.8 MHz. The design is intended as analog IP for integration into larger systems.

This design implements a multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit for 16-bit DLFloat (a custom floating-point format). It accepts two sets of eight FP16 inputs via the ui and uio pins and outputs a 16-bit result in two 8-bit halves over two clock cycles. An external FPGA is required to drive the inputs and capture the output, as the data is presented in a multiplexed manner. A silicon test report confirms functionality, noting a timing discrepancy in the provided cocotb test that was resolved.

This project is a proof-of-concept digital FSK modem with HDLC framing and UART interface, targeting amateur radio packet communication at data rates from 4800 to 64000 baud. It uses a lookup-table-based waveform generator for 2FSK modulation and includes UART flow control signals. The design is intended to be paired with a future CPU to form a complete terminal node controller (TNC). Testing requires external hardware such as an RP2040 or FPGA to validate the interface.

The UART project is a UART data terminal equipment (DTE) implementation in SpinalHDL. It provides standard UART signals such as TxD, RxD, RTS, CTS, DSR, DCD, DTR, and RI, along with interrupt outputs. The design is intended to connect to a standard Tiny Tapeout PCB and interface with an RP2040's UART. Documentation is minimal, with only pin mappings and a brief note that docs are to follow.

The DMTD project is described as a Dual Mixer Timer Differential, but the documentation is extremely sparse elaborating only that it involves I2S and PDM audio interfaces with microphone inputs and beamformed output. The pinout is identical to another audio project, suggesting it may reuse that interface. External hardware required includes microphones, a clock generator, and an I2S receiver. The documentation is essentially placeholder text, providing no real explanation of functionality.

This project is titled DPMU (Dynamic Power Management Unit) and is implemented in SystemVerilog. The pin names are generic, and there is no documentation describing its functionality, interface, or how it should be tested. The clock is specified as 100 Hz, which is unusually low and may indicate an error or a very slow control loop. Due to the lack of documentation, it is not possible to provide a meaningful summary.
